name: Netflix
notice: A layout study, not Netflix: Netflix's signed-out pages rebuilt with Golden Grids by GIFcommit, using public-domain films. Not affiliated with Netflix; the service and its plans are fictional.
summary: Netflix's signed-out home page and a title page, rebuilt as stacked golden grids around twelve films of Weimar cinema. A ranked row of ten becomes two grids in which rank sets size, and one film is opened scene by scene.

reviewed.method: Captured signed out at 390, 820 and 1440 pixels. The signed-in browse page redirects to a login and was not captured.

real: The twelve films, 1920 to 1929, with their years and directors. All are in the public domain in the United States, where this study is hosted; six appear to remain protected in Germany.
The stills and clips, which are frames from those films.
invented: GIFcommit as a streaming service, with its plans, prices, reasons to join and questions. None exists.
The ranking of the ten films, the synopses and every caption.
The sign-up form, which sends nothing.

assets.source: Cut from prints on the Internet Archive and Wikimedia Commons (captures/stills.sh in the source records each one). Some prints are restorations of uncertain origin.
assets.licence: public domain in the United States

owner: Netflix, or the estates and archives that hold the films
